text:
maria: Hey all — quick question about CLI creds in scripts. My team uses OS keyring locally but CI sets REDWOOD_API_KEY. We want a small helper script to: 1) prefer env var in CI, 2) fallback to ~/.redwood/credentials (keyring-backed), and 3) support export for ephemeral containers. Any patterns?

alex: +1 to explicit order. In bash I use a tiny loader:
```
# load-creds.sh
if [ -n "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" ]; then
  echo "using env"
else
  # prefer file then fallback to keyring
  if [ -f "$HOME/.redwood/credentials" ]; then
    export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(grep '^api_key=' "$HOME/.redwood/credentials" | cut -d'=' -f2)
  else
    # mac/linux keyring call
    export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(secret-tool lookup service redwood-api user "$USER" || true)
  fi
fi
```

jamie: For CI we bake the env into the pipeline secrets and then do `unset REDWOOD_API_KEY` at the end of the job. If you need to pass creds into a container, prefer mounting a temp file with mode 600 instead of env var when the runtime supports file secrets. :lock:

maria: Nice. Any tips for the `rwd` CLI profile migration? We have a few legacy `profiles` files floating around.

alex: I wrote a tiny helper that converts old profiles -> credentials file:
```
rwd profile list --json | jq -r '.profiles[] | "name:\(.name) api_key:\(.token)"' > ~/.redwood/credentials
chmod 600 ~/.redwood/credentials
```

patrick: One gotcha: don't call keyring from root in CI images (keyring libs often fail). If you need noninteractive auth in containers, generate a short-lived token via service account and set it to REDWOOD_API_KEY and rotate daily. We reuse `rwd token create --ttl 24h --out /tmp/token` in our deploy scripts.

devex-bot: Reminder: validate no creds in git history before merging scripts. `git-secrets` or a pre-commit hook helps. :warning:

maria: Thanks everyone — I'll prototype loader + converter and ping for code review.
